c74object.name: didddle~
c74object.description: Splits a mono audio signal from a bowed or plucked string instrument (bass, cello, viola, violin or guitar profile) into one signal per sounding note, plus a residual. It runs the fidddle~ pitch detector internally, so the profile, calibration and detection attributes behave exactly as in fidddle~. Every output is delayed by the same fixed amount (the latency message and attribute), and voices plus residual add up exactly to the delayed input.
c74object.discussion: How it works. Each voice is modelled as a stack of harmonic partials at the pitch the detector reports. Every partial is fitted to the spectrum with the exact window shape, so partials of different notes a few bins apart are pulled apart coherently. Where partials of two notes coincide (octaves, fifths, thirds) the shared energy is split by each note's own spectral envelope. Each voice is then gated to its note, and the unpitched attack of a new note (the pluck click or the start of a bow stroke) is handed to the voice that starts. The residual. The residual is defined as the delayed input minus all the voices, so nothing is lost: bow noise, notes the detector missed and sounds that are not pitched all end up there. To prove it, delay a copy of the input by the reported latency, invert it and sum it with all seven outputs: the result is silence (see the help patcher). Latency. The shortest delay is one analysis window (about 85 ms for a cello at 48 kHz). The detector needs roughly that long again to be sure of a new note, so with the shortest delay the first part of an attack may stay in the residual. A larger latency attribute waits long enough that the attack is assigned too; beyond about 150 ms there is little further gain. Limits. Octaves and unisons share all their partials and cannot be split reliably from a single channel; the result there is a plausible, not exact, division. Separation quality follows detection quality: a missed or false note is a missed or false voice.

entry.name: signal
entry.description: Outlets 0-5: audio of voice slots 0-5. Outlet 6: the residual. All share one delay.

entry.name: list
entry.description: Outlet 7: midinote velocity slot, as from fidddle~. A velocity of 0 is a note-off. These follow the detector and are not delayed by the latency.

inlet.description: Mono audio signal, ideally a close-miked or pickup signal. Also accepts the messages reset, info and calibrate.

outlet.description: Audio of the note holding voice slot 0, delayed by the latency. Silent while the slot is free. Slots are persistent per note, not sorted by pitch.
Audio of the note holding voice slot 1, delayed by the latency. Silent while the slot is free. Slots are persistent per note, not sorted by pitch.
Audio of the note holding voice slot 2, delayed by the latency. Silent while the slot is free. Slots are persistent per note, not sorted by pitch.
Audio of the note holding voice slot 3, delayed by the latency. Silent while the slot is free. Slots are persistent per note, not sorted by pitch.
Audio of the note holding voice slot 4, delayed by the latency. Silent while the slot is free. Slots are persistent per note, not sorted by pitch.
Audio of the note holding voice slot 5, delayed by the latency. Silent while the slot is free. Slots are persistent per note, not sorted by pitch.
The delayed input minus all the voices.
A list of three integers. Velocity 0 means note-off.

Messages in response to info (profile, calibration, latency, analysis, timing_us) and calibrate progress messages. A latency message (samples, milliseconds) is also sent whenever the object is rebuilt.

method.name: reset
method.description: Discards all tracking state and rebuilds with the current attribute values.

method.name: info
method.digest: Report profile, calibration, latency, analysis and timing
method.description: Sends from the right outlet: profile (name, voices, minfreq, maxfreq), calibration, latency (samples and milliseconds: the delay of every output relative to the input), analysis (sample rate, detector window, separator window) and timing_us (the detector's mean and maximum analysis time per hop in microseconds, the hop budget and the number of dropped events).

method.name: calibrate
method.digest: Learn the open strings of your instrument
method.description: Identical to fidddle~: calibrate 1, then pluck or bow each open string on its own; calibrate 0, calibrate cancel, calibrate clear. See the fidddle~ reference.

attribute.name: latency
attribute.description: The delay of every output relative to the input, 0 to 2000 ms. 0 uses the shortest delay the analysis window allows (about 85 ms for a cello at 48 kHz, longer for lower instruments). A larger value gives the detector time to confirm each note before its audio is emitted, so attacks land in the right voice and the sound of a note is complete from its first sample. Voices plus residual always equal the input delayed by this amount. Changing it rebuilds the object.

attribute.name: transient
attribute.digest: Attack length given to the new voice (ms)
attribute.description: How long after a note starts the unpitched attack (pluck click, bow noise, jete bounce) is given to that note's voice instead of the residual, 0 to 300 ms. 0 keeps attacks in the residual. Default 80.

attribute.name: profile
attribute.description: Selects the instrument: 0 bass (plucked 5-string electric), 1 cello, 2 viola, 3 violin, 4 guitar, 5 contrabass (bowed and plucked double bass). Sets voices, minfreq and maxfreq to that instrument's defaults and adapts the analysis window and harmonic model. Same as in fidddle~.

attribute.name: voices
attribute.description: The most notes separated at once, 1 to 6 (output slots). The profile sets this (4 for bass, cello, viola and violin, 6 for guitar).

attribute.name: minfreq
attribute.description: The lowest fundamental frequency searched, 20 to 2000 Hz. A lower value needs a longer analysis window and so adds latency.

attribute.name: maxfreq
attribute.description: The highest fundamental frequency searched, 100 to 6000 Hz.

attribute.name: minlevel
attribute.description: Notes quieter than this level are ignored, -90 to -20 dBFS.

attribute.name: confirm
attribute.description: How many analysis frames a new pitch must persist before a voice starts, 2 to 24.

attribute.name: release
attribute.digest: Time before a voice ends (ms, 0 = profile)
attribute.description: How long a note may go unsupported before its voice ends, 50 to 1000 ms. 0 uses the profile's own value.

attribute.name: retrigger
attribute.description: How much louder the partials of a ringing note must become for a repeated pluck to retrigger it, 3 to 30 dB.

attribute.name: calibration
attribute.description: Produced by the calibrate message and saved with the patcher; see fidddle~. Send calibrate clear to remove it.
